html:
The fall of the Berlin Wall was the night of 9 November 1989, when East German border guards opened the crossings in Berlin and crowds poured through. It became the symbol of the end of the Cold War.

East Germany had built the Berlin Wall in 1961 to stop its people from fleeing to the West. More than a hundred people were killed trying to cross it.

By 1989 the Eastern Bloc was cracking. Mikhail Gorbachev, the Soviet leader, had made clear he would not send tanks to save the old regimes. Hungary opened its border with Austria, and thousands of East Germans escaped that way. At home, huge peaceful protests filled the streets of Leipzig and other cities.

On the evening of 9 November a government spokesman, Günter Schabowski, read out new travel rules at a press conference. Asked when they took effect, he said, wrongly, that they applied at once. The news was broadcast in East and West. Thousands gathered at the checkpoints, and the guards, without clear orders, let them through. People climbed on the Wall and began to chip pieces off it.

  • It was one of the revolutions of 1989 that ended communist rule across Eastern Europe.
  • Germany was reunified less than a year later, on 3 October 1990.
  • The Soviet Union dissolved in 1991.
sum: The fall of the Berlin Wall was the night of 9 November 1989, when East German border guards opened the crossings in Berlin and crowds poured through. It became the symbol of the end of the Cold War.
